resale_co.name: Certificate of Continued Occupancy (CCO)
resale_co.issued_by: Cranford Fire Department, Bureau of Fire Prevention & Risk Management
resale_co.lead_time: Not stated. Give at least two requested inspection dates; inspections are between 4 and 5 p.m. on business days and are confirmed by the office.
requirements: Ten-year sealed battery or hardwired interconnected smoke alarms on each level and in the bedroom area, including basements and finished attics
Carbon monoxide detection in all sleeping areas, and wherever the home has a fuel-burning furnace or boiler or an attached garage
House numbers clearly visible from the street, securely fastened, weatherproof and on a contrasting background (a sign within 25 feet of the street if the house is set back more than 150 feet)
Sump pumps must discharge to a storm sewer or the street gutter line, never into the sanitary sewer
Homes with a generator, solar panels, battery storage or other secondary power source need a printed (not handwritten) label within 18 inches of the main electrical panel and the electric meter
All building permits must be closed (final inspections through the Building Department) before the certificate is issued
Buildings must comply with zoning for their area

resale_co.how_to_apply: Apply online through the Township's SDL Portal (a free account is needed): choose Certificate of Continued Occupancy under Online Requests, enter the property, put at least two requested inspection dates in the comments, and pay through the portal. Or fill out the paper CCO application (June 2025 form) and leave it with payment in the drop box at the Fire Department, 7 Springfield Avenue. Checks are payable to Township of Cranford; major credit cards are accepted with a fee. The certificate can be picked up, emailed or mailed.

resale_co.notes: In Cranford the residential CCO is run by the Fire Department and is the same certificate that covers the state smoke and carbon monoxide requirement; Ordinance 2025-07 (Code Section 223-11 A) folds the smoke/CO certificate fee into the CCO application fee. Change of tenant (rental) CCO is $50. Commercial CCOs go through the Cranford Building Department. Other phone numbers on the requirement sheet: Engineering (908) 709-7218, Building Department (908) 709-7213; the June 2025 form lists the Zoning Officer at (908) 709-7213 while the March 2025 requirement sheet lists (908) 709-7216. The SDL Portal needs an account, so the paper application is listed as the application link.

requirements: Ten-year sealed battery or hardwired interconnected smoke alarms on each level and in the bedroom area, including basements and finished attics
Carbon monoxide detection in all sleeping areas, and wherever the home has a fuel-burning furnace or boiler or an attached garage

Handled as part of the Township Certificate of Continued Occupancy inspection (sump pump, house number, open permit and zoning items are checked at the same time)

fire_cert.notes: There is no separate smoke certificate fee for a sale: Ordinance 2025-07 sets the smoke/CO inspection fee at $50 (up from $35) and says it is included within the $100 CCO application fee. The CCO forms do not list a portable fire extinguisher.
